monthly_review.summary: This month shows a deliberate shift toward lower-intensity, higher-volume aerobic base work — evidenced by reduced HR, slower pace, and increased Z1/Z2 time — though total volume and session count are meaningfully lower than last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone distribution shifted dramatically: Z1+Z2 now accounts for 86% of this month’s time (vs 55% last month), while Z4/Z5 dropped from 19% to 0% — indicating a conscious, almost exclusive focus on aerobic recovery and base building.

goal_tracker.message: You need 11.8 more km across 4 remaining sessions — averaging 2.95 km per run — to match last month’s distance. To exceed it, aim for 13.0 km across those 4 runs (avg 3.25 km).

insights.title: Efficiency declined despite lower HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency dropped from 13.66 to 13.09 m/sec per bpm — meaning you’re covering slightly less ground per heartbeat at similar or lower intensities. This suggests either form inefficiency during longer/slower efforts (e.g., 9.5 km @ 10:33/km, stride length 66.5 cm) or under-recovery affecting neuromuscular coordination.

insights.title: Near-total absence of threshold and VO2 max stimulus
insights.body: Zero time in Z4 (anaerobic threshold) or Z5 (VO2 max) this month — compared to 15% and 4% respectively last month — indicating loss of race-specific fitness maintenance. Your best recent pace (428 sec/km = 7:08/km in April) has not reappeared this month.

insights.title: Cadence improved but stride length decreased under fatigue
insights.body: Cadence rose from 142 to 143 spm overall, yet stride length dropped notably during the long run (66.5 cm @ 10:33/km) vs shorter runs (e.g., 71.1 cm @ 9:13/km on 5/13). Ground contact time also spiked to 351 ms on the 9.5 km run — up from ~309–316 ms on fresher days — suggesting form breakdown late in endurance efforts.

insights.title: Aerobic TE is stable but insufficiently distributed
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE is 2.7 this month — down from 3.1 — and all five recent runs show TE ≤3.0, with no sessions above 3.2. While consistency is good, the lack of ≥3.5 TE sessions (which drive mitochondrial biogenesis) limits aerobic capacity gains.

recommendations.action: Do a 45-min Zone 2 run (HR 128–138 bpm) tomorrow, focusing on maintaining cadence ≥145 spm and stride length ≥70 cm — use real-time cadence alert on Garmin.
recommendations.reason: Your recent runs show cadence improves with freshness (150 spm on 5/13), and Zone 2 is where you spend 47% of time — optimizing form here builds durable aerobic economy.

recommendations.action: Insert one 20-min progressive run this week: start at Zone 2 (130 bpm), build to upper Zone 3 (152 bpm) for final 8 min — target avg HR 142 bpm, pace ~530–540 sec/km.
recommendations.reason: Reintroduces threshold stimulus missing this month (0% Z4); matches your April avg HR (142) and bridges the gap between current Z2 dominance and prior Z3/Z4 work.

recommendations.action: After your next run >6 km, perform 3 × 1-min strides (90 sec walk recovery) at ~428 sec/km (7:08/km) pace — monitor vertical oscillation (<7.5 cm) and ground contact (<310 ms) via Garmin metrics.
recommendations.reason: Your fastest recent pace is 428 sec/km (5/05), and strides preserve neuromuscular speed without high HR load — critical to prevent decay of race-pace efficiency.

weekly_focus.description: Maintain high-volume Zone 2 foundation while reintroducing subtle threshold and neuromuscular cues to protect efficiency, pace range, and running economy.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 endurance run (45–60 min, HR 128–138 bpm)
Progressive tempo run (20 min, ending in upper Z3)
